plain_what: Instead of a grid of independent numbers, each 4x4 block of a weight matrix is one quaternion, a four-number turn-and-scale, applied by the Hamilton product. Trained quaternions are then snapped to 120 exact icosahedral rotations plus a small scale, so a block product becomes a table lookup and a few shifts and adds.
how_it_works: Compact form: each projection map (attention q/k/v/out, recurrence in/gate/out, MLP gate/up/down) is stored as Q[out/4, in/4, 4], one quaternion per 4x4 block, so 4x fewer weights. A block acts as the Hamilton left-multiplication matrix L(a,b,c,d) = [[a,-b,-c,-d],[b,a,-d,c],[c,d,a,-b],[d,-c,b,a]]; an output quaternion is y_j = sum_k Q_jk (x) x_k with the input read as in/4 quaternions (16 multiply-adds per block, so no arithmetic is saved on its own). Snap: each trained quaternion becomes m * 2^e * (g1 + g2/4), where g1 is the nearest of the 120 unit icosians (the binary icosahedral group 2I, exact over Z[phi]), g2 the icosian nearest the residual, m a 2-bit mantissa in {1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75} and e a power of two: about 19 to 20 bits against 128 for f32. A product of two snapped quaternions is a read in the 120x120 Cayley table plus shifts and at most two adds. Activations can be snapped to the same set after training. Trained-in snaps used a straight-through gradient; the GPU snap itself was a matmul against the 120 icosians. The forward first expanded each map to a dense matrix for cuBLAS, then used a fused Hamilton kernel (OP2); both are retired in favour of SpiralCore/FBS selection.
geometry: Quaternions and the Hamilton product; the 120 unit icosians = binary icosahedral group 2I = 600-cell vertices; exact Z[phi] coefficients; the 120x120 Cayley (group) table; spin double cover (sign kept exactly).

status_reason: Quaternion weights and 2-bit-mantissa icosian pairs met their bars (1.5148 BPB, level with dense; docs/labs/icosian-mantissa-2026-10-11), but only as a dense Hamilton-block contraction run through matmul, which D25/D30 ban; the code that ran them now refuses. Single-icosian snaps and trained-in activation snaps lost. The mechanism stays open.
reopen_conditions: A table or Cayley-product path (120x120 read, shifts, adds) that contains no dense all-input contraction, for example the block product applied only to blocks chosen by routing, as #2279 did for projections; it must be a new D37 sheet (fresh FIT, owner release, separately scanned float module, export gap reported).

An explicit architecture decision for a Hamilton-block trunk: the 18 Oct architect audit says the active discrete model has no dense projections to replace, so reopening is a new architecture. The 18 Oct optimization path already lists 'spinor/quaternion adapters' as a conditional, measured-ceiling-only item.

Before any negative on activation snapping counts, a soft-to-hard schedule (blend alpha*snap + (1-alpha)*x with alpha rising to 1) compared with the post-hoc +0.0196 BPB, as pre-registered in the activation-snap record.

A served-form table kernel for exact-set x exact-set block products, measured in tokens/s on the same CUDA harness, with weight bytes per token held equal to the dense control (8.55 MB vs 8.62 MB in the rung-0 study).
At least 2 seeds with paired per-block analysis (noise 0.0012-0.0041 BPB in these records) and fresh transfer for any KEEP (D22).

rule_compat.D11: Weight side multiplier-free by design (two icosian table entries, a shift, at most two adds); the activation side and the exact x exact table kernel were never built, and export of quaternion-weight models is refused (quaternion_served_refusal).
rule_compat.D23: No softmax or squashing in the mechanism itself; snaps use nearest-point selection.
rule_compat.D30: Failed as run: the forward expanded each map to a dense matrix and called cuBLAS, and the snap itself was a matmul against the 120 icosians. The OP2 fused kernel is a handwritten dense block contraction, which D25 does not accept as a replacement. Both execution paths now refuse.
rule_compat.D32_D37: The historical form is float and was frozen by D32; D37 allows it back as an offline float sheet by re-registration. Exact quaternion/icosian actions with integer-pair Z[phi] coefficients or finite transition tables are named in D32 as a discrete substrate; the active model uses 8D signed-axis transport instead.

Tokens/s, wall-clock or energy of any quaternion or icosian map; Q256 uses the same 5,537,792 float multiply-adds per token as D256.
A soft-to-hard schedule for activation snapping, or a finer direction set (third icosian term, or the 2,160-point second E8 shell).
Any width larger than 256 or any run longer than 2,000 steps; the 4x-fewer-weights penalty (+0.088 BPB) was measured only there.
Device parity for the OP2 fused kernel (parity tests exist but were skipped; no named device receipt).
A fresh-transfer measurement for the quaternion or icosian KEEPs (D22 asks for one; none is recorded in the lab records).
Quaternion maps used inside a routed or selected structure instead of an all-input sum.
failed_only_on_configuration: Single-icosian snaps (+0.141 post hoc, +0.140 trained in): only 120 directions about 15 degrees apart; the residual pair cut mean angle to 4.73 degrees and recovered most of it.
Power-of-two norm (+0.055 over an f32 norm): too few levels; a 2-bit mantissa removed it (+0.004).
Trained-in activation snap with a straight-through gradient (+0.0231 vs post-hoc +0.0196, about 2x noise): one gradient bridge at one scale; the pre-registered soft-to-hard schedule is untried.
4x fewer map weights at equal width cost +0.088 BPB: a capacity trade at width 256 and 2,000 steps, not a refutation.

The dense contraction itself was retired by rule (D25/D30), not by a negative result; on 13 Oct three '*snap*' unit tests that exercise it were reported failing by design (recurrence-geometric-gates record); I did not re-run them.

Do the rung-0 gains (equal weight bytes, +0.018 BPB over dense) survive at scale and under D37 offline float training with an export gap?
